definitions.explanation: A mythical creature from Japanese folklore said to inhabit rivers and ponds. Typically depicted as humanoid with a turtle-like shell, webbed hands and feet, and a dish-shaped depression on top of its head that holds water, which is the source of its power.

examples.english: Kappa are said to live in rivers and ponds.

examples.japanese: {河童|かっぱ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{頭|あたま}→頭：00574_atama⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{皿|さら}→皿：00883_sara⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{乾|かわ}く→乾く：00786_kawaku⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{力|ちから}→力：01661_chikara⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{抜|ぬ}ける→抜ける：02385_nukeru⟧⟦らしい→らしい：09502_rashii⟧。
examples.english: Apparently when the dish on a kappa's head dries out, it loses its strength.

examples.japanese: {河童|かっぱ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{川流|かわなが}れ→川流れ：noentry⟧
examples.english: Even kappa get swept away by rivers (even experts can fail at their specialty)

FOLKLORE:
・Said to love cucumbers (⟦{胡瓜|きゅうり}→胡瓜：05195_kyuuri⟧)
・Known for pulling people into water
・Will politely return a bow (causing water to spill from their dish)
・Associated with ⟦{相撲|すもう}→相撲：00390_sumou⟧ (sumo wrestling)

PROVERBS:
・{河童|かっぱ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{川流|かわなが}れ→川流れ：noentry⟧ (even experts make mistakes)
・{河童|かっぱ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{水練|すいれん}→水練：noentry⟧ (teaching a fish to swim - unnecessary instruction)

CULTURAL PRESENCE:
・⟦{遠野|とおの}→遠野：noentry⟧ in Iwate Prefecture is famous for kappa folklore
・{河童|かっぱ}⟦{寿司|ずし}→寿司：04946_sushi⟧ (cucumber roll) is named after their favorite food
・Featured in many anime, manga, and video games
